This is a social product, and that is what people praise: SOC-COMMUNITY 8 (25.0%, mean 4.88 — tied first); positive social union 11 (34.4%, CI 20.4–51.7%, mean 4.91); SOC-SHARE 3 — spouse, family, students: 'I love connecting with other Streakers on the community page. An app that encourages, uplifts, inspires'; 'The community is a wealth of knowledge & will cheer on + likely inspire more streaks'; 'it's fun to see other family member streaks and their progress (and we even have competitions sometimes too)'; 'The future of social media'; §8.4 the strategic tension — what reviewers praise most is the community, accountability and outcomes; what the company charges for is the number of streaks, 'the private, single-player counter'; what the category commoditises is that counter — 'charge for the part that is hard to copy (a real community, accountability partners, group streaks, the content ecosystem) and stop charging for the part every free competitor already gives away'; §0.8 #2: treat the community feed as the headline product

The social layer's currency is forgeable: 'I feel like people cheat and just put a random number so they're on the discover feature… people still acknowledge those who have a large number of streaks' (NZ, 4★; INT-CHEAT 1) — if streak counts are editable and Discover ranks on them, 'this gets worse — not better — as the community grows'; 'the only item in the corpus whose severity is independent of how many people mentioned it'; open against 25 release notes; §8.2 #6: make streak counts non-editable, or flag edited counts on Discover — close the loophole 'before the community grows into the problem'

claim: The justification made it worse: 'Comment from creator that it encourages people to keep it simple? 🙄' (1★) — a public developer reply arguing the cap is pedagogically good for users 'has been deployed publicly and has landed badly at least once'; §8.1 #4: retire the 'it encourages people to keep it simple' defence in public replies — 'asymmetric downside, and it is free to stop'
this_app_does: public reply defending cap as good for users

claim: The wall is discovered late: both 1★ reviewers met the cap after investing setup effort (MON-PAYWALL-SURPRISE 2, mean 1.00) — 'neither reviewer objects to paying in principle; both object to discovering the wall after investing in setup'; subscription is the only route (MON-SUBONLY 3: 'an unavoidable monthly subscription' — no one-time option acknowledged); §8.1 #3: move the cap disclosure to onboarding — 'The cheapest fix here is honesty about the limit before the third streak, not a change to the limit'

The referral unlock — a monetization instrument nobody mentions: v2.58 (2024-02-28) shipped 'Unlock unlimited streaks when 10 friends join through your invite link', a free route past the exact barrier, and no reviewer mentions it — including the 4★ still complaining about the cap nine months later; outcome unknown: not discoverable at the paywall, ten referrals too high a bar, or removed; 'Given that 7 reviewers are already recommending the app unprompted, a referral unlock that the most motivated advocates do not appear to know about is worth an audit'; research #6

The rename was the one complaint demonstrably acted on: 'Great habit tracker, really unfortunate name' (4★, 2024-01-10, the whole body is seven words; BRAND-NAME 1) — v2.61 (2024-04-23) 'Updated Name and Bug Fixes' renamed Streaking → MyStreaks 3½ months later; reviewers use 'Streaking' before and 'MyStreaks' / 'My Streaks App' after (verbatim): Review | Date | Name used ; 10341126586, 10372917549 | Sep 2023 | "the streaking app", "Streaking" ; 10807436448 | 2024-01-10 | *"really unfortunate name"* — the complaint, 3½ months before the change ; 11900743150 | 2024-11-01 | "MyStreaks app" ; 11919753703 | 2024-11-06 | "the My Streaks App" — whether the review caused it is unknowable, 'but the sequence is clean'

The book, podcast and founders are the acquisition channel: U-ECOSYSTEM-ANY 8 (25.0%) — ECO-BOOK 4, ECO-FOUNDERS 4, ECO-PODCAST 1 — every review in the union is 5★, the only union with a perfect rating, spread from Feb 2021 to Nov 2024: 'This concept, the book, and the app have done a 180 in how I see habits'; 'it wasn't until I found this App + Podcast that I realized how many other areas of life could be positively impacted'; 'Thank you to Jeff & Jami and their team for the great book & app!'; outcome: 'a content channel that delivers users who are already bought into the method before they open the app' — committed long-tenure reviewers (823-day, 900+-day, 'over 2 years' streaks); 'a durable acquisition advantage no habit-tracker competitor can replicate by shipping features'; the caution — the corpus is loud where the product already won and nearly silent about the onboarding funnel where it loses people

The paywall is placed on the commodity, not the differentiator: reviewers praise the community (11, mean 4.91) and outcomes (21) that competitors cannot copy, while the charge is on the streak count that 'every free competitor already gives away' — and the corpus's reviewers know it ('there are so many alternatives that don't make you pay when you've hit a max of 2 goals'; 'if I find a better one I'll definitely switch'); against the common assumption that a cap on the core counter is the natural freemium line, here it is 'a product that cannot do the job at all' for a multi-domain habit practice

Committed long-tenure advocates write the reviews: ADV-RECOMMEND 7 (21.9%, mean 5.00) explicitly tell the reader to download it; ADV-FUTURE 3 optimistic about growth ('crazy good app and I think will be popular over time'); streaks of 823 days, 900+ days, 'over 2 years'; several arrived through the book or podcast — while the three cap complainants are newer users who hit the wall early (at the third streak; before starting)

this_app_does: streak count paid; tip tiers listed

claim: Changing a habit's schedule must never cost its streak record: a reviewer 'had to retire a 6-day streak and start over to change its schedule' because a streak's cadence cannot be edited after creation, and retired streaks cannot be viewed — open after 25 releases; 'Forcing a user to destroy the exact thing the product tells them never to break is a design contradiction' — the record is the asset users most value ('that record is extremely important to me!')
